dossier:
There is no sadder, more beautiful story in international football than the Netherlands. Three World Cup finals — 1974, 1978, 2010 — and three times they walked away empty-handed. Johan Cruyff's Total Football side of 1974 are still talked about as the greatest team never to lift the trophy, which tells you everything: Oranje have spent half a century being admired, celebrated and ultimately denied.

That heartbreak is baked into their identity now, which sounds like a burden but actually makes them one of the most compelling teams on earth. They play with flair and occasional chaos, capable of breathtaking football one half and a baffling meltdown the next. The Dutch footballing culture — Ajax, the academy systems, the obsession with technical purity — keeps producing players of absurd quality, and the current generation might be the most exciting in a generation.

At FIFA World Cup 2026, with matches spread across the USA, Canada and Mexico, Netherlands arrive ranked seventh in the world and quietly desperate. Virgil van Dijk marshals the backline with patrician authority, Xavi Simons dazzles in the pockets between the lines, and Cody Gakpo brings directness and danger out wide. The pieces are there. They always are. The question — as ever with Oranje — is whether this is finally the time the story gets its ending.
whatToWatch: Watch the tension between their instinct to entertain and their desperate need to win — it creates theatre that no other nation quite replicates. When Xavi Simons gets the ball in tight spaces and Gakpo is running beyond, even neutral fans find themselves leaning forward.
xFactor: Xavi Simons — still only 23 but already playing with the composure of a veteran, he has the imagination to unlock any defence and the kind of magnetic brilliance that turns good tournaments into legendary ones.
verdict: Gorgeous, nerve-shredding, and absolutely capable of breaking your heart in the final week — classic Oranje energy.
funFacts: The Netherlands reached the 1974 final without Johan Cruyff ever taking a penalty — he scored one of football's most audacious goals instead, the iconic 'Cruyff turn' making its World Cup debut that tournament.

Oranje's famous all-orange kit was actually not worn in their first 1974 final — they played West Germany in their traditional orange shirts but the colour became so synonymous with Dutch football tragedy that fans now half-joke it is cursed.
name: Netherlands
